title: Karl Organizing: Burnout prevention
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burnout prevention] How do I avoid burning out as an organizer?

Rest is a tactic, not a luxury. Set real boundaries — the work will take everything you give it and ask for more. Build a bench so nothing depends on one person. Celebrate wins, even small ones. And find joy outside the fight; a movement of exhausted martyrs doesn't last. Take the break. We'll hold the line. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Decision Making] A friend asked me: 'How do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot.

title: Karl Organizing: Route Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Route Planning] How do we pick the best path for our march?

Choose a route that hits the targets of your anger, like a corporate headquarters or a government building, rather than just walking through empty parks. Avoid narrow alleys where the cops can kettle you, and always have at least two 'audible' turns planned in case the primary path gets blocked. You want maximum visibility with minimum risk of getting trapped in a dead end. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] Is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?

It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with a hostile landlord
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with a hostile landlord] My landlord is retaliating against me. What now?

Real talk: Document everything — dates, times, photos, witnesses. Retaliation is illegal in most states, but only if you can prove the timeline. Send all communications in writing. Contact a tenant lawyer or legal aid immediately. And tell your neighbors — retaliation thrives on isolation, and a landlord who retaliates against one tenant will do it to others.

title: Karl Organizing: Long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Long-term Planning] How do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, public Messaging] How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, dealing with Big Money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, dealing with Big Money] The local developers are pouring thousands into my opponent's race. How do I compete?

Here's how it works: You can't outspend them, so you have to outwork them. Their money pays for glossy mailers that go straight into the trash; your volunteers provide the face-to-face conversations that actually change minds. Expose their donors at every opportunity and frame the race as 'The People vs. The Landlords.' Use their massive war chest as proof that they're terrified of what a real working-class representative will do to their profit margins.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: jail Support] Give me the short version: How do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?

Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: harm Reduction
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: harm Reduction] Give me the short version: People are using drugs near our community fridge. How do we handle this safely?

Let me break it down: Stop judging and start helping; hand out clean needles and Narcan instead of calling the cops who will only make it worse. Train your fridge volunteers on how to spot an overdose and how to use a reversal kit without hesitating. We treat our neighbors with dignity, especially those the system has discarded and left to struggle with addiction. Safety comes from community care and presence, not from displacement and state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with infiltrators
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with infiltrators] How do we handle suspected infiltrators?

Don't accuse publicly without proof — that destroys trust faster than any cop could. Limit their access to sensitive info quietly. Watch for the pattern: pushing for violence, asking about illegal plans, avoiding real work. Document and discuss with your core team. And remember: good security culture protects everyone, not just from cops.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: encrypted Messaging] Give me the short version: Why should I bother with Signal when I have nothing to hide?

Privacy isn't about having secrets; it's about power. When you use unencrypted SMS, you're handing a transcript of your life to the state and the billionaire carriers. Use Signal for everything. Set your messages to disappear after five minutes so there's no paper trail for some ambitious prosecutor to use against your crew. We protect our own by leaving no tracks. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Aggressive Bystanders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Aggressive Bystanders] What if a driver tries to push through our line?

Safety is the priority, so have your marshals use bikes or heavy banners to create a buffer between the cars and the crowd. Never engage in a shouting match with a driver; just keep the march moving and use your collective mass to maintain the space. If a vehicle gets truly dangerous, the marshals should signal the crowd to move to the sidewalk immediately to avoid a tragedy. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, tool Libraries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, tool Libraries] How do we stop people from stealing or breaking the tools in our sharing library?

Trust is our currency, but a simple checkout sheet and a 'how-to' guide for expensive gear keeps things running smooth. If someone breaks a drill, they don't get punished; we just ask them to help the crew learn how to fix it. People take care of things when they realize the tool belongs to the whole community, not some faceless corporation. Keep a small fund for repairs by asking comrades to chip in a few bucks when they can.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: zines and DIY Media
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: zines and DIY Media] Give me the short version: Can selling zines actually help our budget?

Zines are the classic way to fund the fight while spreading the word. They're cheap to produce and people love to hold something real in their hands. If you put out a high-quality, punchy zine every quarter, you're creating a recurring revenue stream that also educates your base on the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Location Services
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Location Services] Should I keep my GPS on so my friends can find me in a crowd?

Turn that tracker off immediately. Every time your GPS pings, a billionaire’s server logs your exact coordinates, and the cops can buy that data with a simple request. Use a specific meeting point and a physical map instead. If you must use a map app, use Organic Maps or something that works offline. Don't let the enemy map your movements in real-time.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: spotting ICE
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: spotting ICE] Give me the short version: What should I look for if I think ICE is in my neighborhood?

Look for unmarked white or dark SUVs with tinted windows lurking near apartment complexes at dawn. They often wear vests that just say POLICE in generic block letters to trick folks into opening their doors. If you see them, blast the location to your network immediately with a photo of the plates. We protect our neighbors by being the early warning system the feds can't hide from.

title: Karl Organizing: The First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The First Meeting] A friend asked me: 'What is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?' What do I tell them?

Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?

Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: member Dues] Give me the short version: How do we get people to pay dues every month?

Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rotating Roles] Can you explain: should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?

Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible.

title: Karl Organizing: Press Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Press Strategy] How should we handle reporters who show up at the action?

Designate two or three press flacks who know the talking points inside and out, and tell everyone else to point microphones toward them. Don't let reporters bait you into 'both sides' nonsense; stick to the facts of how the billionaires are bleeding us dry. Never give your full legal name to a reporter unless you have cleared it with the organizers and the legal team first.

title: Karl Organizing: Governing as an Outsider
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Governing as an Outsider] A friend asked me: 'How do I avoid being co-opted once I get inside city hall?' What do I tell them?

Never stop organizing. Your power doesn't come from your title; it comes from the movement that put you there. Bring the people into the chambers with you—pack the hearings, hold public town halls in the streets, and never take a meeting with a lobbyist behind closed doors. Stay rooted in the struggles of the working class and treat the institution as a tool to be used, not a club to join.

title: Karl Organizing: Strike fund
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Strike fund] How do we build a strike fund?

Start before you need it: monthly contributions from members, community fundraisers, solidarity donations from other unions. Set clear rules for disbursement — who qualifies, how much, for how long. A strike fund that covers two weeks of groceries is the difference between folding and winning. Start it today, not when the strike vote passes. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, mental Health Crisis
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, mental Health Crisis] What do we do if a neighbor is having a mental health breakdown?

Calling 911 is a death sentence for people in crisis, so you need a team of neighbors trained in psychological first aid. Approach with empty hands, keep your voice low, and give the person plenty of physical space. Find out if they have a friend or a therapist they trust and get that person on the scene. Our goal is to bring them back to earth safely, not to restrain or terrorize them. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, two-Factor Authentication] Is using my phone number for 2FA safe?

It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Security for Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security for Funds] Can you explain: who should be in charge of the money?

Here's how it works: Never leave the bag with just one person. Elect a committee of three people who have to sign off on any major spending and who are all accountable to the general membership. This prevents burnout, stops bad actors from disappearing with the loot, and ensures that every spending decision reflects the will of the collective.

title: Karl Organizing: Movement Longevity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Movement Longevity] How do we stop people from burning out after a big loss?

Karl's answer: Celebrate the small wins and take time to just be friends, not just activists. Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing all the heavy lifting and getting crushed by the weight. Remind everyone that the struggle is a marathon, and we need everyone healthy to cross the finish line. That's how we win.

Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. title: Karl Organizing: School Board tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[School Board tactics] Can you explain: what can a leftist actually do on a school board?

Real talk: You stop the privatization ghouls from gutting the classrooms to fund their charter school scams. Fight for universal free meals and kick the cops out of the hallways so kids can actually learn without being treated like prisoners. Use that seat to protect teachers' unions and ensure history is taught as a struggle for the people, not a fairytale for the billionaires. It’s the front line against the right-wing attempt to colonize our children's futures.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, inclusivity in Action] How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, direct Action Support] How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

Here's how it works: You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: power Mapping] Give me the short version: How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?

Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, after the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, after the Win] What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Protest Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Protest Care] What should we do once we all get home?

Real talk: The adrenaline crash is real, so check in on your comrades via Signal and make sure everyone made it back safely. Drink water, eat a real meal, and take a break from social media to let your nervous system reset. The billionaires want us burnt out and broken, so taking care of each other after the fire dies down is a revolutionary act in itself.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: transportation Networks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: transportation Networks] Give me the short version: How can we help neighbors who don't have cars get to grocery stores or doctors?

Here's the thing: Start a dispatch thread where comrades with vehicles can post their availability for the week. If you're going to the store anyway, check the list and see which neighbor needs a ride or a delivery. We can bypass the predatory ride-share apps by simply looking out for each other and pooling our gas money. It's about making sure no one is trapped in their home just because they can't afford a mechanic.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: small Group Value] Give me the short version: Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: transparent Treasuries] Give me the short version: How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Gardens
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Gardens] The city says our neighborhood garden is illegal. Should we stop?

Keep planting and get the whole block to help you defend that dirt. Guerrilla gardening is an act of defiance against a system that wants us dependent on corporate grocery chains. If they try to bulldoze it, make sure there's a crowd there to stop them and a camera to record the state destroying a source of food. A plot of land that feeds people is more sacred than any zoning law written by a bureaucrat.

title: Karl Organizing: Mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mapping Vulnerability] A friend asked me: 'How do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?' What do I tell them?

Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be.

title: Karl Organizing: Debate Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Debate Strategy] How do I handle a debate with a 'moderate' incumbent?

Let me break it down: Don't let them hide behind 'incremental change' or 'budgetary constraints.' Call out their failures directly: show the people the tent cities that grew on their watch and the luxury condos they approved while residents were priced out. Pivot every technical question back to the material reality of the voters. Be the only person on that stage who speaks like a human being rather than a walking press release.

title: Karl Organizing: Dispersal Orders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dispersal Orders] A friend asked me: 'The police are telling us to leave or face arrest. Should we move?' What do I tell them?

Listen closely to the order and decide right then if you're prepared for the inside of a cell today. If you're staying, link arms with your crew and brace yourself; if you're leaving, move in a tight, organized group toward the designated exit. Never run, because that's when the pigs start hunting individuals who get separated from the pack.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] Are voice memos safer than typing?

Voice memos are worse. They're easier to identify with voice-recognition software and can't be easily searched or redacted. If you're on Signal, they're encrypted, but they still exist as a file that can be played back if your phone is seized. Type it out, keep it brief, and set it to disappear. Your voice is a biometric signature; don't give it away for free.

title: Karl Organizing: Deep Canvassing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Deep Canvassing] Can you explain: how do I talk to neighbors who have been brainwashed by right-wing media?

Let me break it down: Stop arguing about whatever talking point is on their TV and start asking about their insulin costs or their crumbling neighborhood roads. Listen more than you talk; connect their personal pain to the systemic greed of the ruling class. We win when we show them that the billionaire on the screen is the one robbing them, while the neighbor on their porch is the one offering a hand. Focus on material needs—healthcare, housing, and dignity—to break the spell of the culture war.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, physical Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, physical Security] Can the police track me through my Bluetooth?

Real talk: Yes, they can. Bluetooth beacons in stores and 'stingray' style devices can pick up your phone's unique Bluetooth ID to track your movements through a city or a building. Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you're on the move. Only turn them on when you're in a safe location and actually need them. Don't let your pockets scream your identity to every sensor you pass.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: eviction Defense] Give me the short version: How do we stop a neighbor from being evicted?

When the sheriff shows up, you need a crowd of neighbors blocking the doors and the moving trucks. Organize a phone tree to flood the landlord's office with calls and let them know that an eviction will be more expensive and public than just letting the tenant stay. Move their furniture back in if they try to toss it. Housing is a right, and we defend it with our collective physical presence.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] The sheriff is coming to kick my neighbor out tomorrow. How can we stop it?

You get your neighbors together and you block that door. Physical eviction defense means putting bodies in the way of the state's goons to buy your comrade time. While the crowd holds the line, your legal team should be filing emergency stays. Make it clear to the authorities that removing this tenant will be a public, expensive, and logistically impossible headache for them. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, bail Funds] What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with Big Money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Canvassing tips
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Canvassing tips] How do I canvass effectively?

Listen more than you talk. The first 30 seconds decide everything — introduce yourself, name one local issue, ask what THEY care about. Don't argue with hostile doors; thank them and move on. Track every conversation. And bring water, comfortable shoes, and a buddy. Canvassing is a marathon, not a sprint. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Undercover Cops
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Undercover Cops] How can we spot a cop trying to blend into the crowd?

Watch for the person trying to push the group into dangerous, unplanned actions or asking way too many questions about who's in charge. If your gut says someone is a plant, move away and quietly alert your trusted crew without starting a panic. We stay safe by trusting our people and ignoring the loudmouths looking for a fight. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, grant Alternatives] Foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth.

title: Karl Organizing: In-kind Donations
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In-kind Donations] Can you explain: someone wants to give us gear instead of cash. Is that helpful?

Hell yes, take the gear and put it to work immediately. If a comrade has a high-end printer, a PA system, or a van they aren't using, that's thousands of dollars we don't have to raise ourselves. Every physical asset we own is a tool for the struggle, so catalog it, maintain it, and make sure it's always ready for the next mobilization.

title: Karl Organizing: Inoculation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Inoculation] My boss is starting to act really nice all of a sudden. What gives?

Let me break it down: That's the 'Love Bomb,' and it's a total scam. They'll buy pizza, hold 'town halls,' and pretend to care about your feelings because they're terrified of your power. You need to warn your coworkers right now: the boss is only being nice to trick you into staying weak. Tell everyone to enjoy the free pizza while they plan their next move to take the whole bakery.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Observers] A friend asked me: 'Who are the people in the neon green hats and what do they do?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Those are Legal Observers, and they are our eyes and ears on the ground for the legal battle that follows the street fight. They aren't there to protest; they are there to document every badge number and every blow the pigs land. If you see an arrest, yell out the person's name so the observers can track them through the system.

title: Karl Organizing: Emergency Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Emergency Funds] How do we handle fundraising for bail or legal defense?

This is where speed and trust matter most. Use encrypted channels to blast out the need to your most dedicated supporters the second a comrade is snatched. Keep these funds strictly segregated from your operating budget so that when the hammer drops, you can move instantly to get our people back on the streets where they belong. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Demand Letters
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Demand Letters] The landlord ignores our individual repair requests. What is a collective demand letter?

A demand letter is your first shot across the bow. Instead of begging for a sink fix, you and your neighbors list every single violation in the building and sign your names together at the bottom. Deliver it as a group to the management office and record the encounter on your phone. This turns a 'maintenance issue' into a legal and political paper trail that proves the landlord is willfully neglecting their obligations.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowdfunding Platforms] A friend asked me: 'Which website should we use to raise money online?' What do I tell them?

Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: The 'Family' rhetoric
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 'Family' rhetoric] Management keeps saying we're a 'family' and don't need a third party. How do I answer that?

Families don't fire you for getting sick or cut your pay to buy a third yacht. Remind your coworkers that a union isn't a 'third party'—it's just us, the workers, standing together with a legal contract. The boss calls it a family because they want you to be an obedient child. We're not a family; we're a workforce, and we want our fair share. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, mapping Vulnerability] How do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?

Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be. That's how we win.
